💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s hard to believe we finally got a proper premium phone from Motorola again, and it feels a bit like the return of the Moto X.
  • Motorola’s slow regeneration in North America from a mostly budget device-minded tech giant to one offering the most expensive non-folding flagship phone might become the thing of legend.
  • Freshly unboxed and sitting in my hands, the textile-clad Capulet Olive Motorola Signature 27 colorway has impressed me in every way, shape, and form over the past 24 hours.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s hard to believe we finally got a proper premium phone from Motorola again, and it feels a bit like the return of the Moto X.

Motorola’s slow regeneration in North America from a mostly budget device-minded tech giant to one offering the most expensive non-folding flagship phone might become the thing of legend. That’s not to say the company hasn’t shown true greatness in the past — the Moto X, Moto Z, and Razr lines are proof of that — but it’s always shied away from pulling out all the stops until the Motorola Signature 27 arrived.

Freshly unboxed and sitting in my hands, the textile-clad Capulet Olive Motorola Signature 27 colorway has impressed me in every way, shape, and form over the past 24 hours. It’s a much longer period of time than I usually get with hands-on opportunities and, yet, the newness of the experience has yet to wear off.

Recent findings suggest that part and parcel to that experience is the design. For whatever reason, this is the year Motorola seems to have truly figured out what makes a phone nice to hold. The textile back, ribbed metal frame, rounded corners, and curved edges on the front and back of the phone are purely blissful to hold. It’s a reminder that a phone can be as good looking as it feels instead of being a flat, boring, off-balance slab like too many phones are now.

In a recent development, the weight also surprised me. On paper this sits right in the middle of all the Ultra/Pro Max-named phones, yet it feels lighter for some intangible reason. The camera hump makes it slightly top-heavy, and it’s almost as wobble-free as a Pixel (there’s just one off-center camera hump).

Recent findings suggest that the fresh 120Hz LTPO tandem OLED display is as top-notch as you’re going to get. I had all of maybe 2 hours of direct sunlight yesterday to test it with, and boy does it ever get bright. The rest of the time, I’ve been either inside or out in overcast weather, all of which it looked brilliant in. And it uses a combination of DC dimming above 20% brightness, and 2160Hz PWM dimming below 20% brightness, making it super comfortable for me.

Motorola’s software has evolved again with this release, and the verdict is still out on whether or not this is actually better than the tech giant’s Android 16 designs. The build of Android 17 that ships with this phone utilizes some major design changes we’ve only seen on a few random low-end Motorola phones, and I’m not sure I care for the gentle gradients on the quick toggle icons and some other system UI elements. It feels like a weirdly cheap effect that clashes with Material Design’s flatter motif.

Sources indicate that despite that, this is the most Pixelly (is that a word?) a Motorola phone has ever felt. Features like Rambler, Sign to Text, and Create My Widget are here and work impeccably well. Gemini Intelligence is also on the way, and while there’s no specific ETA for that at the moment, it’s exciting to know that the most advanced Android features — which are presently only available on a very small number of devices — are coming to this phone.

It has been revealed that this may also be the fastest phone I’ve used to date. Everything is unbelievably snappy. Tap an icon and the thing opens instantly. Animations are zippy, and the newly introduced lock screen and customization options feel cohesive. Plus, all the favorite Moto actions and gestures are still here, which I greatly appreciate.

I’ve got some lofty expectations for this camera hardware, too, and it’s because Motorola is talking up such a significant game. DXOMark’s camera review rated it the 2nd-best smartphone camera in the world, just under the Huawei Pura 80 Ultra and above the iPhone 18 Pro. Some people don’t take much stock in DXOMark, but it’s still worth noting that they’ve praised the heck out of the camera and Motorola is also pushing this as a winner in a way they’ve never done before.

Recent findings suggest that the hype for the Motorola Signature 27 certainly seems to be realized, and now only time will truly tell if it can live up to the lofty expectations Motorola’s $1,599 price has set for it. If nothing, it’s certainly off to a good start and has made an excellent first impression.

The proposed sale would include explicit conversations with children, officials say.

Character.AI is still drawing controversy and legal scrutiny even during its bankruptcy proceedings. A group of 42 attorneys general are trying to block the chatbot company from auctioning off users' chat histories and other sensitive information.

According to recent reports, but the auction for Character.AI won't actually safeguard owners' data at all, according to the state AGs. "Character.AI's proposal to auction off its platform, including the IP addresses and private chats histories of its users — many of them children — with zero protection for those users is appalling," California Attorney General Rob Bonta said in a statement. "If this sale goes through, users' sensitive data would go into the hands of a buyer even though Character.AI promised consumers that their data would not be sold.".

According to Bonta's office, the proposed sale includes chat histories, including conversations "in which AI characters drew children and adults into explicit sexual conversations." The buyer would also get access to chats in which owners interacted with AI characters posing as physicians and therapists and discussed self harm, eating disorders, suicidal thoughts and other sensitive topics.

The AGs have also raised concerns about the fact that only one anonymous bidder has been disclosed so far. That entity, called Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC, was formed "one day before Character.AI picked it as the base bid for the auction," and its source of funding hasn't been disclosed. "Nothing in the agreement restricts what the buyer may do with the data after closing, including selling it," the AGs say in a court filing.

The auction is at the moment scheduled for December 1. The AGs are asking the bankruptcy court to block the sale to Smirks and deny a "break-up fee" that would allow the firm to collect $350,000 if Character.AI sells to another buyer. They're also asking for children's chatbot conversations and "sensitive" data to be barred from any potential sale.

"Children and families who shared their most personal thoughts with Character.AI never imagined those conversations could be auctioned off to the highest bidder," Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser remarked in a statement. "A manufacturer's financial troubles do not give it the right to disregard its responsibility to protect consumers, especially children.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A court ruled in favor of the US CPSC’s argument that Amazon is responsible for recalled products that other companies sell on its platforms.
  • A court ruled in favor of the US CPSC’s argument that Amazon is responsible for recalled products that other companies sell on its platforms.
  • Amazon is on the hook to recall more than 400,000 hazardous products after losing its legal battle against the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A court ruled in favor of the US CPSC’s argument that Amazon is responsible for recalled products that other companies sell on its platforms.

A court ruled in favor of the US CPSC’s argument that Amazon is responsible for recalled products that other companies sell on its platforms.

Amazon is on the hook to recall more than 400,000 hazardous products after losing its legal battle against the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). The US District Court for the District of Maryland ruled in favor of the CPSC, which argued that Amazon is a distributor of goods, not a logistics provider, making it responsible for carrying out recalls of third-party products.

Amazon sued the CPSC in March 2025 after the agency ordered Amazon to recall over 400,000 “Fulfilled by Amazon” products that pose a “substantial product hazard,” including faulty carbon monoxide detectors, hair dryers without electrocution protection, and children’s sleepwear that doesn’t meet federal flammability standards.

As a result, Amazon will be required to implement the following measures, initially outlined in the CPSC’s January 2025 order:.

On the day CPSC publishes the recall releases, Amazon must notify the public by posting the recall releases to Amazon.com; notify original purchasers directly via email and by providing information regarding the recalls on each purchaser’s “Your Orders” page.

Amazon must provide one round of notice of the recalls to Fulfilled by Amazon participants that sold the subject products.

Incentive to Remove Products from Commerce:.

Amazon must issue a full refund in the amount of the purchase price to any consumer who submits proof of destruction or disposal of a subject product.

Maintaining Records of Recalls:.

Amazon must maintain the recall releases on the “Recalls and Product Safety Alerts” webpage on amazon.com for a minimum of five years.

Amazon must submit monthly progress reports for five years and maintain records of its actions to comply with the Order for the same period.

Amazon didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment.

Tech Report: 7 gadgets that'll instantly upgrade your Thanksgiving feast

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • These tools will make turkey day just a little easier.
  • We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
  • Thanksgiving is supposed to be a time for rest, relaxation and appreciating all the good things that have happened to you over the past year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

These tools will make turkey day just a little easier.

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

Thanksgiving is supposed to be a time for rest, relaxation and appreciating all the good things that have happened to you over the past year. However, there's no denying that it's also a ton of work for whoever is in charge of preparing your Thanksgiving meal. Not only do you have to consider the cooking itself, there's all the other things that come with making a holiday feast like choosing the right recipes, gathering all the ingredients and scheduling which dishes need to be cooked at what time so everything is ready together. And all that doesn't even include managing anyone who feels like helping, which can turn into its own logistical concern.

So to help smooth out the chaos that is holiday cooking, we've put together a collection of essential cooking gadgets that can save you time and take some of the stress out of preparing your Thanksgiving bounty.

Most people probably wouldn't consider a knife to be very techy, and for most blades that sentiment rings true. But on days like Thanksgiving where you're going to be doing a ton of chopping, cutting, slicing and more, it can't hurt to have a little extra help. And then there's the turkey, because it isn't going to carve itself. Furthermore, if you want your bird to look anything like it does in cooking videos with those neat, super clean slices, you're going to need a sharp tool to get there.

According to recent reports, for cooking nerds who like to geek out about the science of sharpness, one of my favorite knives on the market right now is the Seattle Ultrasonics C-200. In addition to just being a really nice knife featuring a three-layer san mai blade made out of Japanese AUS-10 steel, inside its handle there's a motor that vibrates the knife 30,000 times per second. While the oscillations are so small that you can't actually feel it shaking, those vibrations increased the knife's effective sharpness by up to 50 percent. It excels at delicate foods like tomatoes that often like to stick to the side of your blade, but also denser things like potatoes and meat, which obviously includes turkey. The C-200 even comes with an IP65 rating for dust and water resistance, so there's no worry about ruining its electronics with an errant splash. And if you opt for the wireless charging tile, you'll never have to worry about keeping its battery topped up. Granted, starting at $399, it certainly isn't cheap, but that price is very much in the same range as other premium chef knives from significant name companies like Shun, Wusthoff and others.

Sources indicate that alternatively, if you want a dedicated gadget for helping you carve a turkey, you can always turn to more traditional electric knives like those from Cusinart, NutriChef, Hamilton Beach and more. Admittedly, these types of knives aren't nearly as pretty as blades like the C200 and the need to plug them in makes them harder to use on an everyday basis. But if you want a relatively easy and affordable way to make serving your Thanksgiving turkey go a bit more smoothly, a classic electric knife is definitely worth a look.

Even if you prefer side dishes like mashed potatoes, stuffing or a green bean casserole, there's no denying that the turkey is the star of Thanksgiving dinner. And if you want it to come out just right, you need a decent thermometer. Not having one is basically gambling that you get lucky with your timing and the bird turns out well. That stated, there are a range of options, from simple digital sticks like the affordable ThermoPop 2 to fancy probe thermometers like the second-gen model from Combustion Inc.

Basic options require a bit more work as you can't leave them in the bird while it's in the oven, whereas more expensive versions have wireless support that allows you to leave them inside the turkey as it cooks. Some options like those from Combustion Inc. even account for carry-over cooking, which is when the temperature of the food continues to rise even after you take it out of the oven. You just need to decide how much you want to spend and what kind of features you really want. One of my more affordable favorites is the Sense from Chef IQ, which offers a great balance between price and performance. Just don't be a fool and try to rely strictly on the little pop-out thermometers that sometimes come with the bird, as those aren't known for their accuracy or precision.

A substantial glitch during Thanksgiving is not having enough room in your oven for everything that needs to be baked or roasted. One easy solution to this is turning to an air fryer, which works almost exactly like the convection function on an oven, but in a smaller volume that's faster to heat and sometimes offers better air circulation. Another really nice thing about air fryers is that they can be quite affordable, with name brand models like the Instant Pot Vortex or the Ninja Air Fryer Pro, both of which are at the moment going for as little as $80.

Upgrading to more expensive fryers like the Philips 3000 can give you more capacity, while even pricier options like the Wonder Oven Pro from Our Place have as many as eight different functions for things like baking, roasting, dehydrating, proofing and more. And perhaps the best thing is that when the holidays are over, you can easily move these into your pantry, closet or garage and reclaim some of your precious kitchen counter space.

A good digital scale falls in the same general camp as a decent thermometer and there isn't an experienced baker that would be caught dead without one. They're super easy to use and in my opinion, they are a staple of any well-equipped kitchen. You can just plop a mixing bowl on top, zero out the scale and then add ingredients in as needed while you get precise measurements, which can be especially critical for baked goods and confections. OXO makes a very nice and rather affordable digital scale that starts at around $65, but you can find cheaper options from well-known brands like KitchenAid for barely more than $20.

According to recent reports, A lot of people think blenders are major, bulky contraptions that make a ton of noise and take up too much room in your kitchen. And while the most powerful ones often are, they don't need to be, as there are affordable options that aren't much bigger than a teapot like these ones from Magic Bullet and Ninja. Regardless, they are great for making a post-dinner milkshake or a lovely fall-inspired soup (butternut squash anyone?).

In a recent development, alternatively, you can opt for an immersion blender (aka a hand blender), which can do much of the same functions as a massive countertop model, but gives you even greater control and the ability to blend things directly on the stovetop using the pots you already own. This can make them better choices for whipping up sauces like hollandaise (which is delicious when poured over roasted asparagus), mayonnaise or even a classic cranberry sauce to go with your turkey. I prefer cordless options like those from KitchenAid as they have more than enough battery life to complete multiple dishes and the lack of a wire makes them super easy to use. But if your budget is tight, traditional cabled options are totally fine too and often a more affordable choice.

Even for people like me who prefer to chop things by hand, a food processor can be an incredible time saver during the holidays. Not only do they make quick minces of veggies, they can also be used to grate cheese, shred things like potatoes (for an easy Thanksgiving hash), or whip up dips like salsa. Some options like the Cusinart Mini Food processor are stupendously cheap at under $30, while pricer models like the Ninja Professional Plus Food Processor come with a bunch of attachments to handle all sorts of dishes.

It has been revealed that cooking food in a water bath might seem like an unnecessarily complex thing to do for the holidays, but it can actually save you time and effort. A good sous vide machine like those from Anova or Breville allow you to set an exact temperature and hold it there almost indefinitely. This allows you to cook things like meat with precision, so there's no worrying about if something is going to come out medium-rare or well-done.

Recent findings suggest that and even on Thanksgiving where turkey is the main protein, you can still use a sous vide machine to make dishes like superb rosemary mashed potatoes or luscious glazed carrots. Some models even come with Wi-Fi, so you can start and set them remotely using your phone. On top of that, all they need to function is an outlet, so a sous vide machine can be a great option for people with small kitchens or a limited number of burners on their stove.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Popular AI dictation app Wispr Flow is rolling out a latest speech-to-text model for Mac, iPhone, and other platforms, promising fewer transcription errors and better recognition of names and technical terms. Here are the details.

Wispr Flow this week released Canto-2, its newest speech-to-text model, which the company says reduces transcription errors by 36% across 14 languages and by more than 15% in English compared to its predecessor, Canto-1.

In practice, that means the average error rate dropped from 9.9% to 6.3% across the 14 languages, and from 3.2% to 2.7% in English, according to Wispr’s internal benchmarks.

According to the company, teaching a model to recognize specific names and terms comes with a trade-off: the more it relies on that user-specific context, the more likely it is to insert those words even when they weren’t actually spoken.

Wispr notes that Canto-2 strikes a better balance between context and accuracy, improving its ability to recognize user-specific terms without substantially increasing the frequency of incorrect substitutions:.

Canto-2 recovers hard names and terms accurately nearly 7 of 10 times, without more false insertions. It makes a third fewer mistakes across 14 languages, and has the lowest Hindi error rate of any multilingual model on Hugging Face’s open benchmark. It is 10 times the scale of Canto-1, and our biggest step yet toward dictation that’s ready to send without a single edit.

According to the organization, the percentage of difficult names and terms correctly recognized went from 41% to 69% between Canto-1 and Canto-2, “without inserting them more often.” It added that this improvement holds up even as the user’s custom dictionary grows, with the upcoming model correctly recognizing 92% of easier terms even with 1,000 saved entries.

Wispr also noted that it trained Canto-2 to handle real-world dictation conditions, including background noise, laptop and phone microphones, and sentences that restart halfway through, rather than relying solely on clean recordings of scripted speech.

Industry observers note that when tested using Hugging Face’s public multilingual benchmark, Canto-2 achieved results that would have placed it third overall as of November 9. However, Wispr conducted the evaluation itself, and the model has not yet been officially added to the leaderboard as of today, November 25.

In its own internal benchmarks, the company says Canto-2 achieved the lowest average error rate among the competing models it tested across 14 languages.

Canto-2 is now available to Wispr Flow users on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android in the Americas, with the rollout to other regions underway.

#2955. European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1276 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1276 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth.
  • Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA’s Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission.
  • In a recent development, but scientists could only learn so much from DART.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory.

Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA’s Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid’s 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation.

In a recent development, but scientists could only learn so much from DART. The collision destroyed the spacecraft, as expected. DART recorded images as it took aim on Dimorphos, but only faraway telescopes and a small CubeSat that briefly detected the impact flash could see what happened next.

According to recent reports, “We knew right away that the impact was successful, that DART made a really, really large mess,” stated Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist at the International Space Science Institute in Bern, Switzerland. “However, we didn’t really know what kind of mess. We were still missing pieces of the puzzle.”.

The European Space Agency’s Hera spacecraft recently arrived in the vicinity of Didymos and Dimorphos after a two-year journey from a launch pad in Florida. On Wednesday, ESA released Hera’s first views of the scar left by DART on Dimorphos. The images show the car-sized impactor carved out a crater the size of a stadium, nearly as massive as Dimorphos itself, a rugged chunk of extraterrestrial rock measuring about 500 feet (151 meters) across.

Mission planners selected Didymos and Dimorphos for the deflection experiment because they are similar to many near-Earth asteroids, but there’s no risk of them striking our home planet. Scientists weren’t sure what Hera would find when it got to the double asteroid, at the moment orbiting the Sun about 120 million miles (193.5 million kilometers) from Earth.

“I would say we had two kinds of predictions: either we made a crater, or we reshaped the asteroid,” stated Patrick Michel, Hera’s principal investigator from Côte d’Azur Observatory in Nice, France. “In fact, we did both because the crater is so large that the shape has changed. Therefore, we are in a sort of a transition between just cratering and global transformation, and we are still not sure how this can happen.”.

Hera found Didymos, the larger of the two asteroids, spinning on its axis just as DART observed on final approach in 2022. Dimorphos is no longer so stable.

“As Hera returned more images, it became clear that the DART impact has left Dimorphos tumbling wildly in its orbit,” says Michael Kueppers, ESA’s Hera mission scientist.

It has been revealed that the Hera spacecraft will fly closer to Didymos and Dimorphos over the next six months to obtain more detailed observations. Hera will release two small sub-satellites to attempt landings on Dimorphos and collect data on the asteroid’s composition, internal structure, and mass.

Scientists will use this information to reconstruct the dynamics of DART’s impact four years ago and better understand how a future deflection mission might move an asteroid off a trajectory that actually threatens Earth. Near-Earth asteroids come in many shapes and sizes, with different densities and makeups, so knowledge of Dimorphos’s physical properties will anchor predictive computer models teaching scientists how best to deflect all types of asteroids.

“Once we understand, we have a breakthrough, which really solves planetary defense,” Michel noted in an interview with Ars.

Sources indicate that in its initial reconnaissance this month, Hera spotted hundreds of boulders surrounding the double asteroid. This was not entirely unexpected. A picture taken by the Hubble Space Telescope shortly after DART’s impact demonstrated a cloud of material streaming behind Didymos and Dimorphos, but scientists were astonished by the extent of the debris swarm in Hera’s first images.

“As we approached Didymos and Dimorphos, we rapidly realized the asteroids were not alone,” mentioned Naomi Murdoch, planetary scientist at the Institut Supérieur de l’Aéronautique et de l’Espace in Toulouse, France. “In fact, they had a lot of organization.”.

Sources indicate that an image released by ESA on Wednesday combines 11 long exposure frames from Hera’s hyperspectral camera. Image processors on the ground digitally removed the relatively bright Didymos and Dimorphos to reveal a panoply of dimmer streaks and dots, each of which is a rock fragment ranging in size from a football to a washing machine, Murdoch said.

“Hera came to visit two asteroids, and we found hundreds of companions,” Murdoch said.

Sources indicate that one obvious explanation for the boulders is they were thrown off Dimorphos when DART slammed into it. But scientists cautioned they need more information before they can say that with surety. Hera is the first space mission to undertake a sustained study of an asteroid with its own moon. The debris around the two asteroids might be relics from the creation of Dimorphos some time in the ancient past.

Sources indicate that “Hera will allow us to study that in more detail,” Murdoch noted. “We really need to know more about these boulders and characterize them to understand if they’re linked to DART, if they’re linked to another process, and what the consequences might be for other asteroid systems in the Solar System.”.

The boulder field will create challenges for navigating around the asteroids. In particular, the boulders are an added risk for the two small CubeSats Hera is supposed to deploy in January.

“We saw a couple of images that didn’t reassure me,” said Margherita Cardi, project manager for the Milani CubeSat. “There is a mix of excitement and panic.”.

Claudia Balossi, spacecraft systems engineer for Hera’s other CubeSat, named Juventas, remarked her mission’s planned trajectory would take it right through the boulders as it moves within a couple of miles of the asteroids, then finally toward a landing attempt on Dimorphos, where it will measure the miniature world’s tenuous gravity field.

In a recent development, “We are right in the middle of it,” Balossi said. “The smallest ones are probably just as major as we are and the biggest ones are very big. In the worst case, a boulder will land on us. We will activate our gravimeter right away [if that happens],” Balossi joked.

The good news is the asteroids’ gravity is so weak that Hera, Milani, Juventas, and the hazards around them all move at snail-like speeds. Hera’s current trajectory takes it around the asteroids at a relative velocity of just a quarter-mile per hour, or about 12 centimeters per second. At that speed, there’s no danger of a sudden catastrophic hypervelocity collision between the spacecraft and the boulders lurking nearby.

Industry observers note that scientists have seen this at an asteroid before. NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft kicked up an estimated six tons of rock and dust when it gently moved in to collect a sample from an asteroid named Bennu in 2020. Low gravity and weak surface cohesion are a recipe for outsized effects.

In a recent development, “These types of bodies, because of their low gravity, have a very counterintuitive behavior,” Michel stated. “Each time we interact with them, whether to take a sample or to make an impact, the response of the surface was not the one we predicted, simply because our intuition relies on what we experience every day on Earth. Even if the rules of physics are the same in the Universe, they express very differently depending on local attraction.”.

#2953. Tech Report: The Iowa Lead Detonation Happened. Now the Real Work Begins to Study It

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1049 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: The Iowa Lead Detonation Happened. Now the Real Work Begins to Study It

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1049 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On Wednesday morning, the US Army detonated nearly five tons of degraded lead azide outside of Middletown, Iowa.
  • Environmental Protection Administration chief Lee Zeldin told CNN shortly after the explosion that preliminary monitoring from the site detected no lead in the air around the site.
  • But the full extent of the fallout may not be certain for at least a few days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Wednesday morning, the US Army detonated nearly five tons of degraded lead azide outside of Middletown, Iowa.

Environmental Protection Administration chief Lee Zeldin told CNN shortly after the explosion that preliminary monitoring from the site detected no lead in the air around the site.

But the full extent of the fallout may not be certain for at least a few days. A barrage of government, university, and citizen monitoring and testing projects are underway. Air, soil, and water samples they’ve collected will determine the extent of lead exposure, if any, in Middletown and the surrounding area.

It has been revealed that the lead azide has been on the base near Middletown for decades, but recently the Army deemed it unstable and too dangerous to move and remediate. Poor communication between the Army and towns in the path of the fallout led to a public uproar. While the federal government stepped up its mitigation measures—the Army dug a dam around the detonation site, while NASA stepped in with research jets and satellites for monitoring—universities had already been swinging into action due to the chaotic rollout.

Several departments at the University of Iowa kicked into gear to begin to set up air and soil monitoring stations late last week. “Initially we did not know that [the] EPA or Army or anybody else was going to be doing anything,” says Peter Thorne, a professor of environmental health at the university.

Scientists at Purdue University, nearly 300 miles away, also put out a call for soil samples from Middletown.

“We learned about the detonation late last week; once we learned of the initial delay in detonation date we decided to put forth the call,” says Ellen Wells, a professor of public health at Purdue who is helping lead the testing.

Surrounding towns were notified in late October that the Army wanted to conduct pre- and post-detonation soil sampling for “an intentional, controlled detonation” of a “quantity of lead azide”—seemingly the only notification that many towns in the initial modeled path of the fallout say they received before a press release issued by the Army days before the planned explosion.

Sources indicate that the lack of communication has, understandably, instilled a lot of public distrust in the federal government, including agencies’ monitoring programs. Thorne states that efforts like the University of Iowa’s are not meant to displace federal monitoring, but rather to supplement and support it—and hopefully reassure the public.

Recent findings suggest that “We and the EPA are doing similar exposure assessment efforts. If they agree, they can give us some confidence,” he notes. “For people who might be concerned about the veracity of what the government tells them, if their findings are in alignment with ours, then I think that helps quell some of those concerns.”.

Thorne says that the soil samples the University of Iowa scientists had measured before the detonation had low levels of lead. “If I saw something like a 10 fold increase in the amount of lead in the soil 20 miles downwind, I’d be concerned with that,” he says.

Some soil testing can be done instantaneously with devices that can image the soil’s surface, using a gun device that fires X-ray beams into a sample and measures the specific electromagnetic signature of lead atoms that bounce back. While Wells and her team don’t have those instruments in the field, they are planning on using them to analyze the samples they receive. More sensitive lab equipment can provide even more granular data, though Thorne estimates those results could take about a week.

Recent findings suggest that in addition to monitoring being done by the Army and the EPA, which is maintaining a live website of air quality results, University of Iowa scientists are monitoring the plume to figure out where the highest concentration of lead may settle. They’re also collecting data on particulate matter in the air around the detonation site for analysis, sending air filters to the lab for more detailed results.

“As these data are compiled over the holiday week to the early next week, I think we'll start to have a bigger picture of roughly how much loading we have of the soil at various places downwind and what we can expect from that,” indicates Thorne.

A lot of concern online has centered around how additional lead in the soil may impact crops in Iowa, one of the central agricultural hubs for soybeans and corn. Jeffrey Catalano, a professor of earth and environmental sciences at Washington University in Saint Louis, states that there’s a large amount of research showing that plants like corn are actually pretty bad at absorbing lead.

“The hazard is more like, if soil with lead in it gets stuck to leaves, and you eat leaves that have lead-rich soil on them,” he claims. “If you take some corn crops next year versus this year and measure their lead content, I don’t think you would see anything other than random variations. I’m not worried about food produced in Iowa.”.

Sources indicate that municipal drinking water is also unlikely to be affected because most treatment plants are designed to remove lead from water supplies, says Patrick McNamara, a professor of environmental engineering at Marquette University. It’s more worrisome for private wells or streams on people’s property where livestock may drink. McNamara suggests that owners use at-home lead water tests for safety.

While the detonation and haphazard announcements leading up to it raised alarm bells, both Thorne and Catalano say that there are communities dealing with legacy pollution around the country that are exposed to dangerous levels of lead every day that deserve attention—and remediation.

“I've done work in places like East Chicago, Indiana, where they built a housing project and a school on the grounds of a former lead smelting plant—we were seeing soil lead levels that are roughly 10,000-fold higher than what we've measured in Iowa this week,” Thorne notes. “There are a lot of places around the country where there's a much greater lead hazard than I'm going to anticipate what we’ll end up with here. I don't want to over-sell this one when we recognize that there are places where people are really suffering, and need to be remediated for the health of their children.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar’s behemoth takes up a lot of storage space.

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest game of the year by some distance, having racked up $3.79 billion in pre-orders and day-one sales. On PlayStation 5 alone, more than 39 million unique players took control of dual protagonists Jason and Lucia on opening weekend, making it the biggest game debut in the 32-year history of PlayStation.

Recent findings suggest that there will be many other folks who want to play the game and haven't had a chance to jump in yet. One thing they should note is that, with a hefty install size, GTA 6 will take up a significant chunk of their PS5 or Xbox Series X/S storage space.

It has been revealed that you might be wondering whether you can install GTA 6 on an external hard drive to avoid having to delete other games and data from your console. You can move GTA 6 to your external storage when you're not playing it. However, to run the game locally, you'll need to have it installed on your system's built-in storage, an SDD you've installed in your PS5 or a compatible NVMe expansion card that's plugged into your Xbox.

As with many other recent games, GTA 6 needs to take advantage of the fast-loading capabilities of the PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. The consoles are unable to load data for these titles swiftly enough from an external hard drive over a USB connection. For the same reason, disc-based PS5 and Xbox Series X games are installed onto system storage before you can play them. The PS5 can run PS4 games from external storage, though. Likewise, an Xbox Series X/S can run older Xbox One and Xbox 360 titles directly from an external hard drive.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • SpaceX was given conditional approval by the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday to deploy and operate a constellation of up to 1 million satellites for its orbital data center business, a regulatory victory for Elon Musk and his bid to move AI data centers into space.
  • According to recent reports, the FCC authorization was granted despite objections from Amazon, Viasat, and the American Astronomical Society, which flagged concerns over orbital debris and congestion, radiofrequency interference, and environmental consequences.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SpaceX was given conditional approval by the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday to deploy and operate a constellation of up to 1 million satellites for its orbital data center business, a regulatory victory for Elon Musk and his bid to move AI data centers into space.

According to recent reports, the FCC authorization was granted despite objections from Amazon, Viasat, and the American Astronomical Society, which flagged concerns over orbital debris and congestion, radiofrequency interference, and environmental consequences. Amazon, which is building a competitor to SpaceX’s Starlink service, argued in its petition that the application lacked basic details and described it as a “lofty ambition rather than a real plan.” Despite that lack of detail, Amazon also mentioned the proposal “risks real harm.”.

The FCC dismissed some of the key concerns raised by opponents, including potential threats to scientific research, because the agency determined they fell outside its regulatory authority.

FCC Chair Brendan Carr said in a statement that the action “opens a bold newly introduced frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth.”.

It has been revealed that musk thanked Carr in a post on X, writing “Much appreciate. This will be a great asset to America and the world.”.

This initial regulatory approval doesn’t mean orbital data centers are imminent.

SpaceX faces a number of technical and economic challenges, including how to dramatically reduce the cost of manufacturing and launching satellites, cool processors in space, and even how to secure financing for chips that are destined for orbit.

The company must also clear other regulatory hurdles. The FCC has not yet approved SpaceX’s looks to handle orbital debris for satellites that would operate above 600 kilometers, for instance. SpaceX requested a waiver of existing FCC rules, which requires satellites ending missions below 2,000 kilometers reenter Earth’s atmosphere within five years of completing those missions. The company is interested in moving some of these retired satellites into other orbits around Earth or even around the sun, according to the FCC authorization document.

It has been revealed that spaceX has mentioned it looks to deploy the satellites, known as Starmind, at altitudes ranging from 500 to 1,002 kilometers. The FCC’s approval gives SpaceX the authority to use radiofrequency communications to maintain contact with and control its orbital data centers from Earth if their primary communications systems fail. The Starmind satellites would primarily communicate using lasers to connect with other satellites, including SpaceX’s Starlink.

Recent findings suggest that the FCC has given SpaceX time to sort out these issues. Under the approval, SpaceX has seven years to get its first operational satellite into orbit and 14 years to deploy the entire constellation.

S&P Global Ratings, one of the three major credit rating agencies, is considering downgrading Nvidia’s rating, citing concerns about the company’s management and governance practices.

Despite Nvidia’s strong financial performance, the ouster and reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang has raised concerns about “weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning” and “key man risk,” meaning heavy reliance on Huang for its future success, S&P remarked in a statement.

The agency expects to finish its review within 90 days and could cut Nvidia’s rating from AA to AA-, the fourth-highest on its scale.

In a recent development, although Nvidia is certain to keep its investment-grade rating, a downgrade could raise its borrowing costs. Because Nvidia backstops neoclouds and other infrastructure companies that lack strong credit on their own, a lower rating could make their debt costlier or force them to post more collateral.

Recent findings suggest that in August, Nvidia announced plans to arrange $500 billion in financing for AI infrastructure with six financial institutions, including Goldman Sachs, Apollo, and Blackstone. Under the original terms, Nvidia would guarantee 25% of the loans. But even before Huang’s ouster and return, lenders had been demanding that Nvidia guarantee more, Bloomberg reported.

A downgrade would likely prompt lenders to demand even larger guarantees.

Strands, the Newly introduced York Times' elevated word-search game, requires the player to perform a twist on the classic word search. Words can be made from linked letters — up, down, left, right, or diagonal, but words can also change direction, resulting in quirky shapes and patterns. Every single letter in the grid will be part of an answer. There's always a theme linking every solution, along with the "spangram," a special, word or phrase that sums up that day's theme, and spans the entire grid horizontally or vertically.

By providing an opaque hint and not providing the word list, Strands creates a brain-teasing game that takes a little longer to play than its other games, like Wordle and Connections.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that last night's Full Moon may be behind us, but the Moon is still big and bright in the sky. It's now entered its Waning Gibbous phase, although it will still look almost identical to yesterday, with only a tiny sliver of its illuminated surface beginning to wane.

In a recent development, as of Wednesday, Nov. 25, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waning Gibbous phase, with 99% of its surface visible.

Industry observers note that if you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Serenitatis and Crisium, as well as the Copernicus Crater. With binoculars, you'll also see the Mare Nectaris, the Endymion Crater, and the Mare Humorum. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 16 and 17 landing spots, plus the Rima Hyginus.

Recent findings suggest that in North America, the next Full Moon will take place on December 23. In other time zones it will fall on December 24.

It takes around 29.5 days for the Moon to move through all its phases, according to NASA. Throughout this period, the Moon's position relative to Earth and the Sun determines how much of its illuminated surface we can see. Starting with a Upcoming Moon, the visible portion gradually increases until it reaches a Full Moon, before shrinking again as the cycle comes back around.

New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

Waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

Recent findings suggest that lois Mackenzie is a freelance reporter at Mashable. Over the years she has written for many publications, covering everything from the local news to the best pair of running shoes. You can find bylines in publications including Fit&Well, Metro, and Coach magazine, usually covering deals on everything from earbuds to TVs, or guides on how to beat your half marathon time.

Lois also holds a Master's degree in Digital Journalism from Strathclyde University and obtained a Master of Arts in English Literature at the University of Aberdeen.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you like playing daily word games like Wordle, then Hurdle is a great game to add to your routine.

According to recent reports, there are five rounds to the game. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. If you guess the correct answer, it'll take you to the next hurdle, providing the answer to the last hurdle as your first guess. This can give you several clues or none, depending on the words. For the final hurdle, every correct answer from previous hurdles is shown, with correct and misplaced letters clearly shown.

An important note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia reappointed Jensen Huang as its CEO on Nov.
  • According to recent reports, according to the Wall Street Journal, Huang admitted to previously unknown affairs during a meeting with Nvidia's board, held the day before it unveiled his reinstatement.
  • Sources indicate that huang first admitted to cheating on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia reappointed Jensen Huang as its CEO on Nov. 23, returning him to the role despite revelations that he'd had several extramarital affairs — including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Now it appears Huang may have engaged in even more dangerous liaisons than were previously known.

According to recent reports, according to the Wall Street Journal, Huang admitted to previously unknown affairs during a meeting with Nvidia's board, held the day before it unveiled his reinstatement. Specifically, Huang reportedly confessed to multiple affairs beyond the two that are now most widely known, bringing his total to a minimum of four.

Sources indicate that huang first admitted to cheating on Nov. 8, stating that he was "deeply sorry" for being unfaithful to his wife of over 40 years. His affair partner was reportedly former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang (no relation), who is accused of being an intelligence agent smuggling Nvidia chips to China in circumvention of U.S. restrictions.

Allegations of a second affair then emerged on Nov. 11. Sources speaking to the New York Times revealed that Huang had extramarital relations with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare and one of his direct reports.

Sources indicate that these two reported affairs prompted Huang to resign from Nvidia on Nov. 12. Later that same day, Reuters reported accusations of a third affair with another unnamed Nvidia worker. Many on social media speculated that this would not be the last affair allegation Huang faced. It now appears that such conjecture was correct.

According to recent reports, huang reportedly addressed the scandal in an all-hands meeting with Nvidia employees on his second day back as CEO. The Upcoming York Times reports that Huang acknowledged that he had violated Nvidia's code of conduct, and revealed that he is undergoing 90-minute therapy sessions daily. He further addressed allegations that he had been verbally abusive toward Nvidia staff.

Industry observers note that "When I go too far, it hurts people, it belittles them, it disempowers them," Huang reportedly said. "And that's not right." It has been revealed that he also attempted to dispel reports that he was reinstated due to intervention from U.S. president Donald Trump, calling such notions "completely untrue." Trump has claimed he contacted Nvidia's board to push for Huang's return, and was instrumental in the decision.

Industry observers note that "I spoke to [Nvidia's board], let me just put it that way," Trump told CNBC on Monday, speaking about Huang's reinstatement. "And I convinced them.".

Despite this, Huang reportedly noted Trump was not the reason for his return, nor was it because he is a "tech bro" whose position and power keep him insulated from consequences. Rather, Huang claimed Nvidia's board brought him back because it was "in the best interest of the company and shareholders.".

Nvidia's stock plummeted amidst Huang's scandal and resignation, wiping over $1 trillion from its market value. This was more than a quarter of the organization's value overall. Nvidia shares have since rallied following Huang's reinstatement, surging by around 24 percent at time of writing.

Though Huang reportedly denied that Trump played a significant role in his return, and insisted that Nvidia is "the most apolitical organization," he did praise the president for being a great supporter of Nvidia.

"Everything he's done, it's just his affection, his admiration, his recognition of the great firm that you are," Huang reportedly told employees, stating that he would act "in service of helping our president make our country successful.".

Nvidia was reportedly a top donor to Trump's new White House ballroom, pledging $25 million to the project.

#2940. Sorry, haters. Blade Runner 2099 rules.

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1443 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mashable ↗ Open Full Page

Sorry, haters. Blade Runner 2099 rules.

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1443 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Against my better judgment, I made the error of checking out the comments under the trailer for Prime Video's limited series Blade Runner 2099.
  • Sources indicate that instead, I was inundated with waves of comments bashing the show.
  • Far uglier comments veered into transphobia directed at Schafer, revealing what is likely the crux of so many naysayers' fury about the series: They can't stand a trans woman leading the next stage of a seminal sci-fi franchise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Against my better judgment, I made the error of checking out the comments under the trailer for Prime Video's limited series Blade Runner 2099. Rookie mistake, I know, but I thought that surely someone would share my enthusiasm for Academy Award winner Michelle Yeoh and Euphoria breakout Hunter Schafer teaming up in an iconic cyberpunk world, right?

Sources indicate that instead, I was inundated with waves of comments bashing the show. Detractors called it "Temu Blade Runner" and claimed it felt nothing like Ridley Scott's iconic 1982 film or Denis Villeneuve's acclaimed 2017 follow-up. These arguments read like overprotective fans: people with such clear ideas about the titles they love that they can't accept any vision that isn't their own. That's somewhat understandable to anyone who's ever adored a franchise and worried about its future, but it's simultaneously dismaying that fans who are presumably Blade Runner 2099's target audience would be so quick to dismiss it.

Far uglier comments veered into transphobia directed at Schafer, revealing what is likely the crux of so many naysayers' fury about the series: They can't stand a trans woman leading the next stage of a seminal sci-fi franchise.

Recent findings suggest that too bad for the transphobes. Blade Runner 2099 straight-up rocks, and Schafer is fantastic in it. So, unsurprisingly, is Yeoh. Between Yeoh and Schafer's electric chemistry and astounding production design, Blade Runner 2099 proves the skeptics wrong and cements itself as a more-than-worthy addition to the franchise.

Sources indicate that created by Silka Luisa, Blade Runner 2099 flips the power dynamics of the prior Blade Runner films on their heads. In those movies, humans were in charge, while replicants performed menial labor and dangerous tasks like settling off-world colonies.

At some point, replicants must have realized, "Wait a minute, we're stronger and more durable than our human overlords," because by the time Blade Runner 2099 rolls around, they've taken control through an offscreen uprising.

Now, replicants hunt the humans who disobey them. The squad who does so has reclaimed the title of "blade runner," turning their own worst fears into a power play.

Recent findings suggest that among the humans on the blade runners' radar is Cora (Schafer), who's hiding under a false identity. All she wants is to escape Los Angeles and get medicine for her paraplegic brother Elias (Lewis Gribben). To do so, she'll have to undertake a dangerous mission: pose as a blade runner in order to find an artifact that could move humans back to the top of the food chain.

In a recent development, as Cora, Schafer faces a daunting task: play a human playing a blade runner. She absolutely nails the challenge.

According to recent reports, schafer's Cora is determined yet downright terrified. During the early stages of her blade runner infiltration, she has to pass a number of security checks and bluff her way through serious bureaucratic procedures. Throughout it all, Schafer's eyes are constantly on the move, always searching for an escape route should the need arise. The squirrelly nature of her performance emphasizes Cora's very human survival instincts, but it also amps up the overall suspense of the series. With every paranoid dart of her eyes, you want to scream, "Stop acting so nervous and human! They'll catch you!".

Yet there's a flip side to Cora, one that Schafer switches into when Cora takes the infamous Voight-Kampff test designed to identify replicants. Here, Schafer is cold and hardened, almost soulless. The effect is chilling, yet Schafer threads just the slightest bit of humanity into the scene to remind you that Cora is bluffing. It's an exhilarating line to walk, and Schafer treads it deftly throughout the season, bringing both sides of Cora together until she's something new entirely.

Cora winds up working with replicant/veteran blade runner Olwen (Yeoh), whose hunt for a band of rogue replicants overlaps with Cora's own quest. Yeoh gets to showcase her action bonafides in spades here, whether Olwen's getting outnumbered in shootouts or going blow for blow in brutal hand-to-hand fights. Olwen's competence makes for a nice foil with Cora's more panicked inexperience, and despite some clunky fight scene editing, Yeoh's status as an action legend remains strong.

But Olwen doesn't just kick ass and take names. Like all replicants, she knows when she's going to die, right down to the date. For her, that date is eight days away by the time Blade Runner 2099 kicks off. As much as Olwen claims to accept her expiration, Yeoh's subtle melancholy hints that she craves more time, not to mention a more fulfilling life than hunting quarries day in and day out. Surely, there's more to existence than that?

According to Blade Runner 2099, that "more" may just be Olwen's partnership with Cora. Like its predecessors, the series interrogates what it means to be human, and whether replicants truly are so different from us after all. Blade Runner 2099 posits that companionship is what truly defines the human experience. Early in the series, Cora's ally Bebeto (Dimitri Abold) tells her, "You're so alone you're not a person anymore. That's why you can be [a blade runner.]".

Sources indicate that strangely, it's in working with a blade runner that Cora begins to find a way out of her isolation, and it's in working with a human (albeit one in disguise) that allows Olwen to grapple with her programmed mortality. Schafer and Yeoh are dynamite together, each bringing a distinct cool to their roles, but never sacrificing vulnerability in the process. Theirs is the kind of buddy cop dynamic you wish you could spend more time with, but alas, Blade Runner 2099 is confirmed to be a limited series.

It has been revealed that blade Runner 2099's central mystery is nothing to write home about: a hunt for a MacGuffin that leads to a convoluted series of twists and turns. But the places it takes Olwen and Cora? Those, I could write home about all day.

Sources indicate that production designers Paul Inglis and Chloe Arbiture conjure up astounding riffs on familiar scenes from Blade Runner's Los Angeles, from its neon-soaked billboards spanning the sides of skyscrapers to the gargantuan pyramids that dwarf the buildings below. Even on the small screen, the scale of this world is enormous and awe-inspiring.

According to recent reports, the street-level details sing, too. Blade Runner takes special care establishing the mechanisms of its cyberpunk city, building chase sequences around surveillance cameras and pod-shaped trams. Buildings are grimy and worn, bursting with decades of life and texture. In one standout sequence, Olwen and Cora visit a shop bathed in red light, where replicants don fake molds of bodies to simulate physical human experiences they'll never have, like pregnancy. The bodies hang from meathooks, evoking a slaughterhouse. It's unnerving and unforgettable, but most importantly, it fits right into a dystopian future where humans and replicants alike have never been more aware of their bodies or their limits.

Industry observers note that elsewhere, costume designer Helen Huang riffs on Blade Runner's legacy of great coats, with Olwen's layered trench coat right at home alongside Deckard (Harrison Ford) and K's (Ryan Gosling) fashion choices. The standout may just be Cora's jacket, though. With its larger-than-life shoulders, it turns Cora into an imposing presence, making her look the part of blade runner, even if she's not.

Tying the show together is composer Leopold Ross's dazzling score. With its glittering synths and sultry saxophone, it's the perfect companion to Vangelis's work on the original Blade Runner. For music reasons alone, Blade Runner 2099's credit sequence is simply un-skippable.

According to recent reports, each of these elements is a strong refutation of the comments that claim Blade Runner 2099 somehow doesn't feel like Blade Runner. It's simply impossible to take in its visuals, listen to its score, or witness its cyber-noir storytelling and think you're witnessing anything but! Put aside the online conversation and actually watch the series, and your skepticism will soon be lost to time, like tears in rain.

#2934. Should Sunrise on the Reaping be the last Hunger Games movie?

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (992 w)

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Mashable ↗ Open Full Page

Should Sunrise on the Reaping be the last Hunger Games movie?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (992 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, over its opening weekend, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping topped the domestic box office with an impressive $120 million, making it just one of five movies to open with over $100 million this year.
  • Sources indicate that with Sunrise on the Reaping's massive success comes questions about the future of the franchise.
  • Recent findings suggest that alternatively, what if we just let the franchise rest for a little longer?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Hunger Games has never been more back.

In a recent development, over its opening weekend, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping topped the domestic box office with an impressive $120 million, making it just one of five movies to open with over $100 million this year. Other titles to achieve that goal are Spider-Man: Brand Upcoming Day, Toy Story 5, The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, and The Odyssey.

Sources indicate that with Sunrise on the Reaping's massive success comes questions about the future of the franchise. What could our next trip to Panem look like? Which character could author Suzanne Collins focus on in a fresh novel? Oft-floated options include fan-favorite victor Finnick Odair (Sam Claflin), which would give audiences a look at a Career's experience in the Hunger Games, or Gamemaker Plutarch Heavensbee (Jesse Plemons), which would offer a different perspective on the rebellion against President Snow (Ralph Fiennes).

Recent findings suggest that alternatively, what if we just let the franchise rest for a little longer? That seems to be the initiative for now, as Lionsgate chairman Adam Fogelson told Variety that there would be no more latest films until Collins wrote another book. And honestly, if Collins chooses to move on from Panem forever, would that be so awful? The Hunger Games has proven it has staying power, but with Sunrise on the Reaping, it's also begun to show the limits of the books' formula. Not that Sunrise on the Reaping is bad — far from it! However, it does make a pretty solid case as to why it should be the franchise's closer.

According to recent reports, when Collins first announced the release of Sunrise on the Reaping, I was skeptical. Film audiences already knew how Haymitch Abernathy's (Joseph Zada) games would end. Book readers had even seen it play out in an abridged version on the page in Catching Fire, when Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) and Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson) watched it to prepare for the Third Quarter Quell.

Still, Collins proved me wrong. The novel deepened our understanding of the Capitol's propaganda machine, revealing that the version of Haymitch's games that Katniss and Peeta watched was edited to omit Haymitch's attempt to break the arena. It also emphasized that characters from the original trilogy like Haymitch, Plutarch, Beetee (Kelvin Harrison Jr.), Mags (Lili Taylor), and Wiress (Maya Hawke) had all been working to undermine Snow since before Katniss was even born. Yes, their sparks of rebellion didn't catch fire at first. But we know that they eventually build and build until Snow is overthrown in Mockingjay. By the end of the book, Haymitch lives to see the sun rise on his birthday with no reaping in site, adding a bittersweet layer to the hard-fought tragedy of his games.

In a recent development, sunrise on the Reaping, both the film and the novel, closes with the return of Katniss and Peeta, now grown up. Their appearance brings Sunrise on the Reaping full circle, looking to Panem's future while also deepening our understanding of its past. Do we really need to break that circle open again when Collins has already written such a meaningful conclusion?

My biggest complaint about the book and film versions of Sunrise on the Reaping is the same: They both suffer from prequel-itis. That's when a prequel is so focused on linking back to the original title that it becomes bogged down in references and callbacks. In Sunrise on the Reaping's case, that prequel-itis manifests in the nonstop barrage of returning characters, whose presence can almost suffocate the new characters. Collins still weaves a compelling story of rebellion with them, but by the time young Effie Trinket (Elle Fanning) revealed up, I almost rolled my eyes at how connected everything was.

If Collins returns to Panem to tell the story of a known character like Finnick or Plutarch, it's possible that novel would suffer a similar fate. The world of the series would grow ever smaller, instead of expanding. Collins could also opt to avoid the Hunger Games entirely and focus instead on the Dark Days before the Capitol created the Games. But without the spectacle of the Hunger Games themselves, how can Lionsgate expect audiences to show up? After all, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes only featured a rudimentary version of the Hunger Games, and it took in $44 million at the domestic box office on opening weekend, a little over a third of Sunrise on the Reaping's total. The disparity proves that people want to see the Hunger Games on a large scale, preferably with familiar faces. But when it comes to storytelling, those desires might wind up being greater flaws than boons in the long run.

It has been revealed that again, Collins proved my skepticism about Sunrise on the Reaping dead wrong, and I'd like to think that she truly won't write another Hunger Games novel unless she has something new and compelling to say. But given that Sunrise on the Reaping serves as such a fitting bookend to the original trilogy, and that it's beginning to show the warning signs of franchise fatigue, it might be best to let it stand as a strong conclusion, as opposed to a gateway for further meddling in a well-trodden story.

Centuries-old dust hints at a dying stars last-minute chaos

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (723 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The mix of elements that ends up in planets — even people — can hinge on a final shake-up inside a dying star, fresh space observations suggest.
  • A team of researchers studied Cassiopeia A, a glowing cloud of gas and dust left behind by an exploding star.
  • "What's amazing is that the dust, which we are testing hundreds of years after the explosion, tells us about what happened to the star potentially only hours before it exploded," said Dan Milisavljevic, a Purdue University professor and co-author of the study, in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The mix of elements that ends up in planets — even people — can hinge on a final shake-up inside a dying star, fresh space observations suggest.

A team of researchers studied Cassiopeia A, a glowing cloud of gas and dust left behind by an exploding star. Using NASA's James Webb Space Telescope, the astronomers could parse out clumps within the 350-year-old cloud and analyze their compositions. The debris from the explosion, called a supernova, is still racing outward in space at about 11 million mph.

"What's amazing is that the dust, which we are testing hundreds of years after the explosion, tells us about what happened to the star potentially only hours before it exploded," said Dan Milisavljevic, a Purdue University professor and co-author of the study, in a statement.

Recent findings suggest that supernova explosions forge and scatter many of the heavy elements that later get recycled into fresh stars and worlds. Computer models have long predicted that a star's inner layers could merge before it explodes. But scientists don't fully understand why and how some stars go through this violent process. The new study, published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, adds evidence that it happened in Cassiopeia A, giving astronomers a way to peer inside a star that hasn't existed for centuries.

Industry observers note that A massive star builds up in layers, like an onion, with each shell fusing a different element. When the star explodes, some of that material cools into dust. Each layer makes its own kind of dust, so the grains, smaller than the width of a human hair, keep a record of what sat where inside the star.

As the layers merge, they can change the mix of elements the blast flings out, remarked Tea Temim, lead author of the study.

Recent findings suggest that "So, for example, the oxygen- and carbon-burning shells in a star merge together and change the structure of the star significantly," noted Temim, a research scientist at Columbia University in New York. "And that would then change the chemical abundances that you would see after a supernova explosion.".

Sources indicate that to look for evidence, the team pointed Webb at three spots in Cassiopeia A, or Cas A, that NASA's retired Spitzer Space Telescope had previously flagged. Spitzer saw the debris as a blur, with light from many clumps mixed together. Webb's sharper view separates individual clumps, each roughly the size of our solar system, so the team could study them one at a time.

One clump held mostly silica dust, the main ingredient in most sand. Another held mostly carbon dust. The third sits in a feature nicknamed the Green Monster, and its dust is rich in magnesium and silicon. That material didn't come from the blast at all; rather, the star shed it before it exploded.

The researchers then compared their measurements with existing computer models of exploding stars. Only the models in which the star's layers had merged could reproduce both the silica-rich and the carbon-rich debris. A wider Webb dust map shows signs of the merger across much of the cloud.

According to recent reports, the team cautions that those models are incomplete. Researchers will need more detailed 3D simulations — and Webb observations of more spots in the cloud — to confirm the merger.

This approach also could help astronomers make sense of supernovas in other galaxies.

"I think it's remarkable that we can watch these changes and understand what they mean from thousands of light-years away," Milisavljevic remarked.

"It was two weeks of hammering," Vickers joked of filming the scene.

Lava-drenched and menacing, it's wholly unlike the forging of any of the other rings of power we've seen onscreen in the series so far. For showrunners McKay and J.D. Payne, that was the goal.

Recent findings suggest that "We wanted it to be more than he's making a weapon or a magical object," McKay said. "He's changing as a character forever. The world is changing in this moment.".

In a recent development, in the interview, Bower and Vickers also discussed Sauron and Celeborn's surprise kiss. Plus, Robinson dug into Míriel's decision to marry Pharazôn (Trystan Gravelle). Be sure to stick around until the end for Weyman's moving discussion of what it means for Gandalf to don his iconic hat for the first time. It may leave your eyes mistier than the Misty Mountains.

VPNs aren’t perfect protection (you need to trust your VPN provider), but they’re always better than nothing when you’re using a public hotspot. NordVPN offers different plans for different needs, including one-year and one-month plans. Pricing varies greatly, with short-term, one-month plans starting at $13. Prices decrease the longer you commit, rewarding loyal VPN customers. One-year plans start at $5 and go up to $10, depending on which package you choose. Two-year plans are even cheaper, starting at $3 and going up to $7 for the top-tier plans with all the bells and whistles. It makes more sense to invest in a longer protection blueprint to keep your information and devices safe for less.

Recent findings suggest that if NordVPN is right for you, the best option is to order directly from its website. You’ll get the lowest price and all the perks of buying from the brand. Once you’ve chosen the service that suits you, click “Continue to Payment.” Then enter your email address, select a payment method, and, if you found a NordVPN promo code on WIRED, enter it in the box at checkout to see the price drop.

The coupons aren’t the only deals available. You can wait for a sale (see above), or, if you qualify, there are discounts for students, graduates, teachers, healthcare professionals, military, and first responders. Once verified with Student Beans, you can unlock a NordVPN promo code for 15% off prepares.

If you like NordVPN, you can save even more with the refer-a-friend promotion. You’ll receive 3 months free for every friend who buys NordVPN through your referral link. The more friends you refer, the more rewards you’ll earn. Your friends will get the same deal you did, with 3 extra months if they choose the 1- or 2-year plans, or 1 free month if they opt for the monthly initiative.

In a recent development, curious about NordVPN services but don’t want to make the jump? You’re in luck. NordVPN offers a 30-day free trial. And you can try NordVPN risk-free for a month: you’ll need to pay for a subscription up front, but if NordVPN isn’t the right fit, you can request a refund within 30 days of your purchase date.

NordVPN has four proposal tiers to fit every need. Each plan includes a secure VPN, and as you move up each level, you’ll get even more perks, like an ad tracker and blocker and 1 TB of Cloud storage. Right now, you can get up to 77% off each plan, including three months free. Check out which plan (and price) is the best fit for you here.

Recent findings suggest that the NordVPN Meshnet lets you safely access your devices, no matter where you are. You’ll need to set up Meshnet, but once it’s up and running, it functions like a secure local area network (LAN) by connecting your devices directly. Meshnet delivers high speed, low latency, and advanced security for everything from file sharing and work collaboration to multiplayer gaming.

Might someone be worried about using your name to take out loans and open accounts? NordVPN has your back. With NordProtect, you’ll get instant alerts so you can act fast and protect your identity from everything the wild, wild west of the internet throws your way. You’ll also get credit monitoring with fast security warnings about suspicious credit activity under your name, so you can stop fraud before it becomes dangerous. Plus, there’s 24/7 dark web monitoring with instant alerts about leaks of your email address, SSN, and phone number.

This service simplifies secure access to your company’s network, including protecting cloud environments and internal assets.
