📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that an advertiser paid for editorial consideration of this deal. Our editorial experts vetted the deal based on our independent expertise. Because we determined that the deal will save money for our readers, we wrote the content.

In a recent development, SAVE $600: As of Nov. 25, Orion's Black Friday Sale takes $600 (up to 25%) off all sizes of its smart cooling and heating mattress cover, with prices starting at $1,795.

If you love your current mattress but hate waking up drenched in sweat — or arguing with your partner over the bedroom thermostat — this Orion Sleep System deal lets you upgrade your bed's temperature without buying a whole new mattress. For Black Friday, Orion is taking $600 off every size of its smart cooling and heating mattress cover system, with no monthly subscription fee.

The system comes with two main parts: a thin Smart Cover (available in softer or firmer comfort options with a breathable 60% polyester and 40% bamboo top knit) that stretches over any standard mattress between 10 and 18 inches deep like a fitted sheet, and an award-winning, oak-topped bedside Control Tower that plugs into a single outlet.

Sources indicate that the Control Tower circulates temperature-controlled water through anti-leak, tear-resistant tubing inside the cover, maintaining a temperature between 50 and 113 degrees Fahrenheit. Because it uses dual-zone control, each side of the bed can run its own temperature — so one person can sleep at 73 degrees while the other stays cozy at 82 degrees.

Industry observers note that you can set automated schedules in the Orion app, so your bed cools down before you get in, drops lower for deep sleep, and gently warms up before your alarm goes off. There is also a Hot Flash mode that drops your side's temperature before easing back to your schedule, plus a Quiet mode that turns down the tower's sound at night.

According to recent reports, built-in sensors track your heart rate, breathing rate, HRV, and movement without making you wear anything to bed, delivering sleep insights each morning. You only need to top off the tower's water once or twice a year with a purification tablet. And while the cover itself is spot-clean only, you just put your regular fitted sheet over it and wash it as usual.

According to recent reports, if you want a little extra help dialing in your settings, you can add an at-home Sleep Disruption Test (a one-night sensor patch and a quick call with a Sleep Advisor) to find your best starting temperature before you commit. You can also sync the app with Apple Health or Google Health Connect, or pay extra for Orion Intelligence — an optional AI add-on that adjusts your temperature schedule automatically based on your sleep and breathing habits, while keeping all core features subscription-free.

Here's how the Black Friday pricing breaks down across all three sizes:.

Orion Sleep System (Queen) — $1,795 $2,395 (save $600).

Orion Sleep System (King) — $1,995 $2,595 (save $600).

Orion Sleep System (California King) — $2,095 $2,695 (save $600).

Every order ships within seven days with free shipping, a 30-night money-back guarantee with free returns, a two-year limited warranty, 24/7 human support, and HSA/FSA eligibility.

Grab your size from Orion while the $600 Black Friday discount is live.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If it feels like everyone and their dog is watching or streaming Grand Theft Auto VI content, YouTube has the official numbers to prove it.

Industry observers note that in a blog post Tuesday, the company detailed the colossal online impact of Rockstar Games' critically acclaimed blockbuster, announcing that YouTube saw over 3.5 billion global views of videos with GTA 6 in the title on Nov. 19's release day.

To date, the Grand Theft Auto series has over 900 billion views of related content on YouTube, according to the data, with videos specifically about GTA 6 gaining 40 billion views before release day.

Along with YouTubers, streamers across Twitch and Kick broke streaming records with GTA 6 content on launch day. Data from streaming analytics platform Streams Charts said Twitch saw 2.50 million views while Kick had 1.31 million (the platform clocked YouTube at 3.22 million views, less than the organization now reports), marking a reported total of 7.91 million concurrent GTA 6 launch day viewers.

In context, the 24-hour record for most views on one YouTube clip remains with K-pop superstars BTS, whose 2021 "Butter" video saw 108.2 million views in one day, smashing their own 101.1 million-view first-day record for previous single "Dynamite.".

Recent findings suggest that however, GTA 6 can claim the record for most views in a 24-hour debut of a non-music video for the very first trailer released in Dec. 2023: 93 million views in 24 hours.

To mark the streaming news, YouTube added a few GTA 6 themed features to YouTube Live including onscreen Wanted Stars (the stars that pop-up in game if there's police heat on protagonists Jason and Lucia), and a Shorts effect that lets creators use Vice City backgrounds.

Turns out viewers can't get enough of watching others reap the spoils of Leonida — and if you're looking for the best streamers to watch playing GTA 6, Mashable's got you covered.

Latest Update: Not Just Nvidia: Inside Team Trump’s Takeover of Intel

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1906 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The message from the Trump administration to one of the world’s leading semiconductor companies was clear: Give the US government a chunk of your company.
  • Do not make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro told the chief financial officer of the Intel Corporation in August 2025, according to internal notes from a company call contained in a federal lawsuit.
  • Industry observers note that shapiro acknowledged that “the Board could choose not to accept the offer,” according to a summary of his remarks prepared for Intel’s directors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The message from the Trump administration to one of the world’s leading semiconductor companies was clear: Give the US government a chunk of your company. Right now. Or else.

Do not make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro told the chief financial officer of the Intel Corporation in August 2025, according to internal notes from a company call contained in a federal lawsuit. “The President is expecting to announce a deal on these terms on Friday.”.

Industry observers note that shapiro acknowledged that “the Board could choose not to accept the offer,” according to a summary of his remarks prepared for Intel’s directors. But the Trump administration official “noted that rejection will have consequences that [Shapiro] cannot predict.”.

In a recent development, days later, the board gave the administration what it wanted. “It is my Great Honor to report that the United States of America now fully owns and controls 10% of INTEL,” Donald Trump posted to his social platform. “The United States paid nothing for these Shares, and the Shares are now valued at approximately $11 Billion Dollars. This is a great Deal for America.”.

Recent findings suggest that president Trump was similarly jubilant on Monday, announcing that he had “convinced” Nvidia’s board of directors to rehire chief executive Jensen Huang. The proclamation was a shock. But it wasn’t entirely without precedent.

Sources indicate that fifteen months earlier, the Trump administration had interfered with the leadership decisions at another major chipmaker, court documents allege. Then, as now, allegations swirled that the company’s CEO was too close to China. Then, as now, the Trump administration dealt itself into the company’s financial future.

It’s part of a broader shift within the government in general and the Commerce Department in particular, a former member of that department tells WIRED. Out are old metrics “like creating jobs or the US being more competitive or owning more of the market share,” this ex-Trump administration official indicates. When dealing with private companies, a single overriding concern is: “Are you going to give back to the government in cash?”.

Recent findings suggest that documents unredacted as part of a shareholder’s lawsuit against Intel’s board show how far the administration has been willing to go to get what it wants. The lawsuit’s allegations were previously reported by WP Intelligence.

“The Board, operating under the shadow of the President’s threats,” the lawsuit alleges, “caved to the government’s extortion.” A second case, asking for internal records, was filed in April by the same shareholder, Richard Paisner, against Nvidia.

It has been revealed that “It's just straight-up coercion,” states Scott Lincicome, a vice president at the libertarian Cato Institute. “The manufacturer starts making decisions not based on what's best for the company in the short or long term, what's best for shareholders, but what's best for politics and what the government is demanding.”.

“That's not what you want from any manufacturer,” he adds. “When you're talking about the world's most innovative companies and these kinds of bleeding-edge technologies that have not only huge economic implications but national security ones, then that's a huge problem.”.

Sources indicate that representatives for Intel declined to comment for this story. The White House, Commerce Department, and Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment.

It has been revealed that the parallels between Nvidia’s government-assisted autogolpe and Intel’s alleged forced sale aren’t exact. In the Intel case, Trump all but accused the firm’s boss of being compromised by Beijing; in the Nvidia situation, the president reportedly dismissed concerns from his own intelligence agencies about the executive’s connections to China. But both instances show a growing fusion of private enterprise and public office.

During the Biden administration, Intel won awards for up to $11 billion in government grants and contracts, much of it under the CHIPS Act, which was meant to help build semiconductor manufacturing and assembly plants in America and bolster domestic research.

At the time, there was some grumbling inside the Commerce Department, which administered the CHIPS and Science Act grants, about funding what was seen as a “failing incumbent” in the semiconductor space, notes the former official. (Intel had, in recent years, fallen on hard times.) But by March 2025, Intel had received about $2.2 billion of the grants. That’s when President Trump told Congress that the CHIPS Act was “a horrible, horrible thing.” The rest of Intel’s money was put on hold, tied to hitting certain milestones, while the administration said it was renegotiating the deals.

Recent findings suggest that the same month Lip-Bu Tan was hired as Intel’s new CEO. Soon after, his ties to China made him a Trump target, when Reuters reported that Tan had invested in “hundreds of Chinese tech firms,” some with connections to Beijing's military. Tan’s former firm, Cadence Design Systems, pleaded guilty to violating US sanctions by selling semiconductor designs to a restricted Chinese military university, and agreed to pay more than $140 million in fines. Tan was never personally charged, but the violations happened while he was the CEO.

In a recent development, two weeks later, the president was watching Maria Bartiromo’s show on the Fox Business Network. It mentioned a letter a senator had sent Intel about the China ties. Trump posted, "The CEO of INTEL is highly CONFLICTED and must resign, immediately. There is no other solution to this problem.".

Tan went to the Oval Office on August 11 to see if there was, in fact, another solution. He got 40 minutes with the president, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

Tan claimed his experience in China was a strength, not a detriment. According to the book Regime Change, Tan argued that there was no way he could’ve known about every one of the deals his many companies made; Trump, who had his own sprawling business empire, surely knew what that was like. Tan promised to give up his holdings in China, according to a letter Tan shared with Intel’s board, and put any proceeds into a blind trust.

“The primary goal was to eliminate any worries about Lip-Bu himself, his Cadence background and his investments with China,” according to a source with knowledge of the matter. But there were major financial concerns for Intel, too. “We had declining revenues and needed money.”.

Neither Tan’s letter, excerpted in the complaint, nor Trump’s social media posts praising the CEO after the meeting mentioned anything about giving the government a chunk of the company. Yet Trump later insisted that a deal had been cooked up right then and there. “He came in, he saw me, we talked for a while. I liked him a lot, I thought he was very good,” the president told the Wall Street Journal. “I mentioned, ‘You know what? I think the United States should be given 10% of Intel.’ And he said, ‘I would consider that.’”.

In a recent development, “I should’ve asked for more. It was so easy,” Trump later recalled.

According to the court filing’s review of Intel’s internal documents, Shapiro—a former partner at the Newly introduced York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz—made a verbal offer on August 18. Ultimately, in exchange for the cut of Intel, the Trump administration would free up the $8.9 billion US government grants that it had already won. They wanted about a tenth of the company’s stock for free, in exchange for Washington keeping the commitment it had already made.

Then came the call in which Shapiro insisted there was no room for negotiation. “The board needs to consider,” he remarked, according to Intel’s summary of his remarks included in the court documents, the “benefits of having a friend in this administration and what the administration can do to help Intel (including with customers).”.

It has been revealed that intel’s board met, and decided they hated the deal. “The economic terms that had been proposed [by] the Administration were not, in their current form, attractive to the tech giant,” minutes of the meeting, reprinted in the lawsuit, noted.

But they went ahead with it anyway. Paisner’s lawyers say in the court documents the board took the offer thrust forward by the administration. Intel’s attorneys disagree, arguing in their motion to dismiss that there was some back-and-forth deal-making, and it made the agreement more favorable to the company. The grants became “immediately available” while “strategically aligning the interests of Intel’s stockholders and the US Government.”.

Sources indicate that on August 25, Lutnick released a video with Tan, sitting side-by-side on cushioned chairs. “I really look forward to have the US government be my shareholder,” Tan turned to Lutnick and said. “And we can work together and make Intel great again.”.

Industry observers note that inside the company, the video was “a surprise to everyone,” according to a source with direct knowledge of the matter. Some employees joked that it was reminiscent of a “hostage video.”.

Not long after that, Nvidia—led by Tan’s friend Jensen Huang—made a $5 billion investment in Intel. “I love seeing their stock price go up, making the USA RICHER, AND RICHER,” Trump posted. “Who would not want to make deals like that?”.

Deals, plural. On the day Tan was hauled to the Oval Office, Trump declared that his administration had been negotiating separately with Huang. The Nvidia leader was beyond eager to sell more of his semiconductors to China. “And I stated, if I'm going to do that, I want you to pay us as a country something,’” Trump said. They settled on 15 percent of all sales of the H20 model chip. Months after that, they cut a second deal: a 25 percent bounty on sales of Nvidia’s even-more advanced H200 chips.

In their lawsuit against Nvidia, Paisner’s attorneys argue the surcharges amount to “unlawful taxes,” and that the board’s “decisions to enter into such agreements are the product of mismanagement and breaches of fiduciary duty.”.

In court, NVIDIA’s lawyers insisted that the company “did not enter into any illegal ‘agreement’ with the government but instead engaged with the government and stated that it would comply with federal regulations.” Moreover, the attorneys say Paisner is trying to make a political point, rather than a legal one. “When asked about his purpose in bringing this action,” they write, “Paisner was candid: ‘It’s to make a public point of how NVIDIA conducts itself.’”.

Sources indicate that the attorneys wrote this in May, months before Nvidia’s and Huang’s recent drama. Last week, board chair Harvey Jones noted on the tech giant’s quarterly earnings call that it did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” citing his “disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms.” (Not to mention mounting evidence that the company’s most sophisticated chips were making their way to China, in violation of US law.) But, according to The New York Times, after days of pressure from top administration officials, the company and the government essentially struck a deal Sunday night to reinstate Huang.

Industry observers note that “Don’t think for a second that politics ever play a role in this firm, not even a little bit,” Huang stated during his first company-wide meeting after rejoining the company, WIRED reported. “We are the most apolitical company. I don’t love that we talk about politics here. Take it home. I love that we talk about work here.”.

TL;DR: Yes — beds like Sleep Number's ClimateCool and Climate360 pair adjustable firmness with active temperature control on each side, and both are discounted up to 25% through Dec. 7 for Black Friday.

Anyone shopping for a cooler night's sleep eventually runs into the same two questions: Is there an adjustable mattress that actively cools you down, and how does built-in temperature control work alongside adjustable firmness? As it turns out, you can get both in the same bed — and the way it works is completely different from standard "cooling" mattresses.

Industry observers note that if you want to test one out for yourself, Sleep Number's Black Friday sale runs through Dec. 7, with up to 25% off its lineup — including deep discounts on its active-cooling Climate Collection.

Recent findings suggest that most mattresses advertised as cooling rely on passive materials such as gel-infused foam, breathable fabrics, or open-cell airflow layers. Those materials feel cool when you first lie down, and a bedroom fan can help move air across your skin, but passive toppers and covers eventually absorb your body heat and warm up — while a fan cannot reach the heat trapped beneath your back.

Active temperature mattresses solve this by building motorized airflow channels directly into the bed to pull warm air away from your body all night long.

In mattresses like the Sleep Number Climate Collection, the active temperature system sits right alongside adjustable firmness. Instead of traditional metal springs, the bed uses split air chambers underneath layers of supportive foam, letting you dial in your preferred firmness on each side at any time.

Sources indicate that built-in sensors also track your movement while you sleep — so if you roll from your back onto your side, the air chambers automatically soften or firm up under your hips and shoulders to keep your spine level, without interrupting your cooling settings. At the same time, sensors quietly track your heart rate, breathing, and movement in the background (no smartwatch required), rolling everything into a morning SleepIQ score from 1 to 100 in the app.

In a recent development, because both the air chambers and the temperature vents are split down the middle, each side of the bed works independently. On the Sleep Number ClimateCool, a programmable airflow system within a 1.25-inch foam layer pulls excess heat away, lowering the temperature of each side by up to 15 degrees, and it works alongside a breathable cover and 3.75 inches of temperature-balancing comfort foam.

The Sleep Number Climate360 adds active warming into the mix — spanning a 30-degree range from cooler to warmer on each side — and includes 52% more built-in cooling materials plus a smart adjustable base. Both models also run pre-set temperature programs in the app that automatically shift through the night, such as warming your feet at bedtime on the Climate360 before kicking on active cooling during deep sleep.

Struggling to sleep? You might fall into one of these categories:.

Chronic hot sleepers — If you routinely wake up sweating, continuous active airflow keeps heat from building up under your body the way gel toppers and foam pads eventually do.

Couples with different temperature preferences — Because firmness and temperature are set separately on each side, one person can sleep cool on a firm surface while the other stays warm on a softer setup (on the Climate360, one side can actively cool while the other warms).

People with night sweats or temperature swings — Pre-set overnight schedules adjust as you sleep — cooling you down when your temperature spikes or gently warming the bed before you wake up.

If you sleep alone, don't overheat, and already stay comfortable with a bedroom fan or breathable sheets, there is no real need to spend thousands on built-in airflow.

Both models in the Sleep Number smart beds collection are engineered for a 25-year lifespan, come with a 100-night home trial, and are HSA/FSA-eligible — though keep in mind that home delivery and setup fees are non-refundable, and return pickup fees apply if you send the bed back.

Grab your preferred Climate model at Sleep Number before the Black Friday discounts wrap up, and put an end to middle-of-the-night overheating for good.

There's never a convenient time for your car to break down, but a freezing winter morning when you're already running late for work has to be among the worst possible scenarios.

Thankfully, modern automotive technology has made it a lot easier to understand what's going on with your vehicle, often without specialist knowledge or an expensive trip to the repair shop.

Tools once reserved for professional workshops can now connect directly to your smartphone and provide useful information about your car's condition through easy-to-use apps.

TOPDON is one of the companies making this technology more accessible, and offers everything from affordable Bluetooth diagnostic scanners to advanced equipment designed for professional mechanics.

This Black Friday, the manufacturer is launching a substantial sale across its automotive range, with promotional prices running from November 19 through November 30.

One of the simplest ways to prepare for winter is to make sure your car's battery is in good condition before temperatures drop.

The TOPDON BT100 Battery Tester, available for $43.99 during Black Friday, provides a straightforward way to check the condition of a 12V battery without visiting a garage.

It can assess battery health and starting performance to help drivers determine whether a battery might need attention before it leaves them stranded.

Of course, even a well-maintained vehicle can experience an unexpected flat battery, which is why keeping a portable jump starter in the trunk is a sensible precaution.

The TOPDON JS2000 Pro combines a powerful 2,500A peak-output jump starter with a 16,000mAh battery, providing enough power to jump-start compatible vehicles without assistance from another driver.

It also doubles as a portable power bank for charging electronic devices, which could prove particularly useful if you're travelling somewhere remote and your phone is running low on power.

With its Black Friday price of $80.74, it's a practical addition to a winter emergency kit that could come in handy long after the colder months have passed.

Modern vehicles are packed with electronics that continuously track how different components are performing, but drivers often have very little access to this information.

OBD2 diagnostic scanners can connect to your vehicle's onboard diagnostic port and retrieve fault codes to better understand potential problems with your car.

For Android users, the TOPDON CarPal is an especially interesting starting point because it uses Bluetooth to send information directly to your smartphone.

Through the companion app, you can access vehicle health information and diagnostic trouble codes without taking the car to the repair shop for a checkup.

At $37.97 during TOPDON's Black Friday promotion, the CarPal A is also the most affordable diagnostic scanner in the lineup.

Industry observers note that drivers who enjoy carrying out their own maintenance might prefer something more advanced, such as the TOPDON AD600S or AD800BT2, which offer deeper diagnostic capabilities and additional service functions. Both models also benefit from free lifetime software updates.

Another interesting development in automotive diagnostics is the growing accessibility of thermal imaging technology, which can reveal unusual temperature differences that might indicate an underlying problem.

The TOPDON TC002C Duo connects directly to compatible USB-C Android smartphones, iPhones and tablets, essentially turning an everyday device into a portable thermal imaging camera.

It's useful for investigating potential overheating concerns around vehicle components, but its applications extend well beyond automotive maintenance, as it can also identify heat-loss areas around your home.

The TC002C Duo is available for $229.89 during Black Friday, while TOPDON also offers standalone thermal cameras for people who prefer dedicated equipment.

TOPDON’s Black Friday promotion runs from November 19 to November 30, 2026 and covers automotive equipment for casual drivers and professional mechanics alike.

If you've been considering putting together a winter emergency kit or investing in diagnostic equipment, it's worth exploring TOPDON's Black Friday offers before the promotional period ends.

iOS 27.3 is presently in beta testing with developers and public beta consumers. The update includes multiple new features for iPhone users, including the redesigned Health app, iPhone Duo updates, and much more. Here’s everything you need to know about what’s new in iOS 27.3 ….

According to recent reports, 9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

Sources indicate that as my colleague Ryan explained, Apple will likely release iOS 27.3 to all iPhone users sometime in December. Typically, Apple would release its x.2 software updates in December, but this year is different because iOS 27.1 was exclusive to iPhone Duo. That means that, in terms of the timeline, iOS 27.3 is essentially the equivalent of iOS 27.2.

Here’s when Apple has released its December updates in recent years:.

So with that in mind, we expect iOS 27.3 to be released sometime during the first half of December.

Recent findings suggest that the redesigned Health app is back in iOS 27.3. This was first available during testing of iOS 27.2, but did not ship as part of that final update.

The redesigned Health app is split into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The app features an all-newly introduced design that dynamically adapts based on your data, including Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab includes a new Health age feature that uses Apple Watch data to show how your metrics track relative to your actual age.

For Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 owners, it also offers easy access to view your Readiness score every morning.

It has been revealed that for Apple Fitness+, iOS 27.3 adds a new Gym Strength feature. This creates progressive, four-week intends based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment.

As you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weights you logged.

Industry observers note that for iPhone Duo owners, iOS 27.3 adds Reachability support. This setting shifts the interface on the outer display to the right or left, making it easier to reach the far corners. It’s designed to make iPhone Duo easier to use with one hand, despite the wider outer display. You activate it by swiping right on the right edge of the screen or left on the left edge.

It has been revealed that reachability for iPhone Duo is on by default. You can turn it off in Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

Recent findings suggest that iOS 27.3 also brings a fresh face unlock feature to iPhone Duo. This is not full-fledged Face ID. Instead, Apple is using the front-facing camera on the iPhone Duo’s outer display to recognize you, then unlock the device. It doesn’t work for things like Apple Pay and passwords.

iOS 27.3 also tweaks the iPhone Duo’s software keyboard by making the keys slightly narrower and the font slightly smaller.

Finally, iOS 27.3 includes a new option in the Settings app to have your iPhone Duo lock when closed. Once enabled, your iPhone Duo will lock when you fold it, rather than transition content from the inner display to the outer display.

In a recent development, when it debuted, the iPhone Duo included a more robust version of StandBy with fresh clock faces and expanded customization options. iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s StandBy experience to all iPhone models.

This includes the redesigned Analog and Digital Clock faces, as well as additional customization options for colors and complications. The patch also adds support for Shared Albums to the Photos face.

According to recent reports, iOS 27.3 brings several key Siri AI updates. First, the patch expands Siri AI with many fresh capabilities across Apple apps. Apple explains:.

We started rolling out these new capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so consumers can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year.

It has been revealed that there are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

With iOS 27.3, Apple is also starting to test new ways for developers to create Siri AI integrations for the first time. This is described as an “early Developer Preview.” Apple explains:.

Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.

While this is being tested as part of iOS 27.3, Apple claims it will start shipping to customers in a few months.

iOS 27.3 also expands Siri AI to latest languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

iOS 27.3 also introduces usage limits on select Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features. The limits apply to things like:.

Sources indicate that you can unlock higher usage limits with an eligible iCloud+ strategy, starting at $2.99 per month. If you hit your usage limit, basic Siri requests will still work. That includes things like setting timers and alarms.

It has been revealed that iOS 27.3 brings the original set of Apple Intelligence features to China for the first time. This does not include Siri AI or other iOS 27 updates, but it does include the following features:.

iOS 27.3 is a major update to Safari. First, the update adds support for a new vertical tabs design layout on iPhone Duo’s inner display. If you choose this option, your Safari tabs will be arranged vertically along the left-hand side of Safari, rather than along the top. Vertical tabs are also available on Mac and iPad with macOS 27.3 and iPadOS 27.3.

iOS 27.3 also adds a new Adaptive Dark Mode feature. This feature can automatically apply Dark Mode to websites that don’t natively support it. You can choose to have Adaptive Dark Mode automatically kick in or use it on a site-by-site basis.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • You start noticing a bit more scalp in harsh bathroom lighting, a tiny bald spot when you tie your hair up in a ponytail.
  • Beyond skin rejuvenation, clinical studies suggest red-light therapy can help energize hair follicles, increase blood circulation in the scalp, reduce inflammation, and lower dihydrotestosterone levels—a hormone that causes hair loss and thinning.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hair loss isn’t always dramatic. It can be incremental. You start noticing a bit more scalp in harsh bathroom lighting, a tiny bald spot when you tie your hair up in a ponytail. The shower drain is more clogged than usual. Not long ago, hair-loss treatments meant topical remedies, supplements, or a flight to Turkey. Luckily, red-light therapy brings the potential for hair regrowth into your home—no clinical appointment required.

Beyond skin rejuvenation, clinical studies suggest red-light therapy can help energize hair follicles, increase blood circulation in the scalp, reduce inflammation, and lower dihydrotestosterone levels—a hormone that causes hair loss and thinning. Red-light therapy also supports adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production, which helps provide oxygen and blood flow to the scalp and triggers follicles to remain in the hair growth phase.

To determine the best red-light therapy for hair growth, I tapped five WIRED tech reviewers who've dealt with hair loss themselves. We assessed red-light caps, hands-free helmets with full scalp coverage, and low-level laser therapy (LLLT) or photobiomodulation devices for 16 weeks. Along the way, I reviewed the research, spoke with dermatologists, and tracked ease of use. These are the favorites that produced meaningful results and earned our trust.

Be sure to check out our other wellness and skin-care guides, including the Best LED Masks, Best Hair Dryers, and Best Blow Dry Brushes.

I test these devices with several tech reviewers on our team, all of whom have personal experience with hair thinning or loss to different degrees. Most of these at-home gadgets call for a 16-week treatment cycle. We follow the brands' directions and record any visible results along the way.

We monitor changes in hair count, hair density, and scalp health, but effectiveness is only one of the factors we consider. We also judge ease of use, functionality, and comfort. We note the specific wavelengths of light and whether the treatment options feel tolerable or difficult to integrate into everyday routines.

According to recent reports, we also prioritize safety, checking for FDA clearance, automatic shut-off features, and overall durability of the design. To date, our testers have not experienced any side effects, but we would have documented them had they.

I'm testing the Foreo Flip Play and the Theradome PRO Laser Hair Growth Helmet LH80.

Feels a little pointless to look outdoor-ready when you can’t actually use it on the go. It also got too hot for me to wear comfortably. —Nena Farrell.

Does Red-Light Therapy Work for Hair Loss?

According to recent reports, yes—research suggests low-level light therapy can work for certain types of hair loss, such as androgenetic alopecia, also known as male or female pattern hair loss. It can help increase hair count, thickness, and density by stimulating hair follicles and boosting cellular activity in the scalp.

That remarked, results depend heavily on the type and severity of hair loss. Red-light therapy works best in cases of mild to moderate thinning and may be less effective for advanced hair loss or scarring conditions like cicatricial alopecia. Consistency also matters. You typically need regular, ongoing use to maintain results, and benefits can diminish if treatments stop.

What Wavelength of Red Light Is Best for Hair Restoration?

According to the American Hair Loss Association, wavelengths in the range of 630 to 680 nanometers are ideal for hair regrowth. These wavelengths are known to support increased blood flow to the scalp, boost cellular activity, and help reduce inflammation. Some clinical studies specifically cite 650 nanometers as an especially effective wavelength.

Sources indicate that red-light devices that use medical-grade laser diodes tend to deliver more targeted and consistent light than standard LEDs, but both can stimulate hair follicles at the right wavelengths. For best results, look for FDA-cleared devices that list their wavelengths and power output.

How to Use Red-Light Therapy for Hair Growth.

According to recent reports, consistency is the most important part of any red-light therapy routine. Most devices require at least three months of use before noticeable results are observed, and some may take longer. Follow the manufacturer’s instructions, as treatment schedules vary by device, but most recommend sessions three to five times per week. The hair growth is preserved only with continued use, so you’ll need ongoing maintenance sessions.

Sources indicate that always start with a clean and dry scalp so the light can reach your hair follicles without interference from oils or styling products. Some devices include protective eyewear, and if yours does, wear it during treatment. Make sure to wipe the device down with a gentle disinfectant before or after each session to prevent buildup on the LEDs.

Sources indicate that topical regrowth treatments can complement red-light therapy and may help support thicker hair. A few randomized clinical trials suggest that combining minoxidil (2 percent or 5 percent) with red-light therapy can improve hair density and encourage faster regrowth compared to using either treatment alone. For a natural alternative, some research has found rosemary oil to produce results comparable to 2 percent minoxidil for androgenetic alopecia, though the evidence isn’t as extensive as it is for minoxidil.

If you’re pregnant or have an underlying medical condition, talk to your healthcare provider before starting any form of red-light therapy.

Is Red-Light Therapy for Hair Growth Safe?

Yes—for most people, red-light therapy is considered a safe and noninvasive treatment with minimal side effects when used as intended. Still, it's always worth consulting a health care professional before starting any sort of treatment. This is especially the case for anyone with photosensitive conditions or autoimmune disorders that affect light sensitivity.

Industry observers note that I prefer devices that are FDA-cleared because it means they've met certain safety standards for consumer use. But keep in mind that the clearance process is less rigorous than the FDA approval pathway, as it just requires manufacturers to prove their product is “substantially equivalent” to an already legally marketed device. Also, FDA clearance isn't a guarantee of results; it simply means it's considered safe to use as directed at home.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Popular secure messaging app Signal has rolled out a newly introduced update that automatically disables screenshots for the sake of blocking Siri AI from reading your chats. Here are the details.

Signal’s latest app update on iPhone disables a key system feature: taking screenshots.

As Signal told Reuters, that’s because Apple doesn’t presently provide better tools for iOS developers to safeguard app content from Siri AI and third-party AI agents.

By default, owners who update and try to take a screenshot will see a message that says: “Screenshot prevented by ‘Block Siri AI’ setting.”.

Fortunately, there’s an easy workaround. People who want to re-enable screenshots can do so by visiting Signal’s privacy settings and turning off the newly introduced toggle that’s labeled ‘Block Siri AI.’.

Here’s 9to5Mac’s own Arin Waichulis:.

Signal now blocks in-app screenshots on iPhone to keep Siri AI from reading chatsIt’s a upcoming toggle in settings that’s on by default, but can be turned offNo equivalent for its Mac app pic.twitter.com/ImsinqMNPq.

Here’s exactly what that toggle does, per the in-app settings:.

Prevent Siri AI from scanning Signal content. This will also block you from taking screenshots in the app and App Switcher.

According to recent reports, it’s good to see that customers can manually disable the fresh privacy setting if they want. But Signal’s decision to block screenshots does raise notable questions about the potential gap in privacy tools for iOS developers.

Industry observers note that apple already lets you block Siri AI from accessing whichever apps you manually exclude, and that became even easier in iOS 27.2. But rather than directing consumers to that system option, Signal seems to believe it needed to take action itself with this enhancement.

TL;DR: The Pokémon TCG 30th Celebration Elite Trainer Box is on sale for $115.96 at Walmart, down from its previous $237.98 price.

If you had no luck getting an invitation to buy one of the cheaper Pokémon TCG 30th Celebration Elite Trainer Box listings at Amazon before stock ran out, Walmart's latest batch of Black Friday deals has something for you.

As of Nov. 25, the Pokémon TCG 30th Celebration Elite Trainer Box is available for just $115.96 at Walmart, with a hefty $122.02 saving (51% off). Walmart is now barely above TCGplayer's $114.58 market price — with just $1.38 separating the listings. Plus, unlike Amazon’s invite-only listings, these ETBs are readily available without delay.

Factoring in the nine titular 30th Celebration booster packs of trading cards, you're spending roughly $12.88 per Pokémon TCG anniversary pack before accounting for the extras.

These include the exclusive full-art foil Nidorina promo card, 16 foil Basic Energy cards, 65 sleeves, dice, a coin, six dividers, a player's guide, and a Pokémon TCG Live code card.
